text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- U.S. CONSIDERS ILOGIC TO NEGOTIATE FTAA IN STAGES
U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barschefsky said the insistence of the Mercosur trade bloc to negotiate in stages the Free Trade Area of the Americas (FTAA) "is not logical."
-- ARISCO RAISES $150 MLN
Brazilian food company Arisco issued $150 million in eight-year Eurobonds lead managed by Goldman Sachs International. The firm will use part of the money to pay off short-term internal debt.
-- BANKS CUT PROVISIONS AND MAINTAIN PROFITS
Brazil's largest private retail banks maintained their historic profitability in the first quarter of the year due to a reduction in expenses with loan-loss provisions.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- DEPUTIES PRESSURED TO END PROBES INTO VOTE-BUYING SCHEME

A committee of Congress' lower house which is looking into an alleged cash-for-votes scheme has been pressured to report its findings this week by the president of the Chamber of Deputies Michel Temer.
-- WESTERN COUNTRIES DEMAND ELECTIONS IN ZAIRE
The United States, Germany and France want Zaire's new leader Laurent Kabila to hold free elections.
O GLOBO
-- REPORT CONTRADICTS VERSION THAT GIRLFRIEND KILLED FARIAS

A fourth forensic report contradicts the official finding that Suzana Marcolino, Paulo Cesar Farias' girlfriend, killed him and then committed suicide. Farias was the treasurer of former president Fernando Collor.
-- "MR X" TO TESTIFY TODAY ABOUT VOTE-BUYING SCHEME

Former deputy Narciso Mendes, said to be responsible for the recordings of conversations suggesting a vote-buying scheme for the approval of a re-election bill, will testify Monday before a lower house committee investigating into the scandal.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
((-- Fatima Cristina, Sao Paulo Newsroom 5511-2485412))
